assignment.name: Project Progress Report (10%) due by Week 6

rubric.long_description:
• Background and contextual information related to this project, including (1) project vision and goals; (2) project scope and objectives.































• What and how to achieve the project aims: (1) short-term deliverables (to match objectives) and (2) long-time expectations (to match project goals and vision)































• Key stakeholders and interactions (e.g., their roles and tasks, and group collaborations, interaction, and group dynamics, and communication with clients)































• Resources and risks and mitigation strategy (e.g., man-power, materials, equipment, services, time management)

ratings.long_description:
The project introduction clearly explains and meets all the following criteria: 
The overall purpose of the project, its expected outcomes, the key stakeholders' involvements/interactions, and clearly identifies/outlines the resources and risks involved in the project.

The project introduction properly explains and meets substantial majority of the following criteria OR meets all the criteria but with some ambiguity. 
Criteria: 
The overall purpose of the project, its likely outcome, the key stakeholders' involvement/interaction, and clearly identifies/outlines the resources and risks involved in the project.

The overall purpose of the project, its likely outcome, the key stakeholders' involvement/interaction, and clearly identifies/outlines the resources and risks involved in the project.

rubric.long_description:
System Specifications































• User stories and major project requirements- clear identification of functional and non-functional project and user requirements and accordingly design and define corresponding user stories.































o Identification of the functional and non-functional requirements expressed in each user story































o Presentation of all the completed user stories designed based on specific functional or non-functional requirements. Each user story should be the smallest unit of work to satisfy specific functional or non-functional requirements instead of a combination of several &amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;user stories&amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; clearly described and designed based on client&amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;s needs testable and estimable (the corresponding acceptance criteria can be described here but will be assessed based on the criteria in the testing section).































• Demonstration of the implemented user stories, including:































o the implemented user stories in accordance to the project aims and scope, and justify how they meet client requirements































o how well (quality) the most crucial user stories are implemented































o It can include high-level designs (e.g., mock-ups, UIs)































• Detailed documentation of































o all aspects being selected for the project, including links to all relevant evidence for completion from GitHub (e.g. Relevant code, Jira issues);































o Any other details that demonstrate the system specification and design that might be specific to the nature of the project (e.g., API integration, empirical evaluation of algorithms).































System Architecture and Design































• Initial system architecture and design (both text descriptions and diagram illustrations)































o High-level system component diagrams clearly articulate system components and their functionalities































o Design patterns or off-the-shelf frameworks being used along with relevant diagrams































o How the system being designed and implemented































o Main technical components of the system































o Detailed explanation on how different components interact































o Clear statement of which components/parts are developed by the group, and which ones are adopted/utilized or need to integrate with.

Thorough understanding of the user requirements and insightful and cohesive user stories, and feasible system/solution specification and design.

Extensively and clearly address the majority of the criteria, the presentation is of good clarity and readability, and clear and explicit articulations on the majority of the required aspects and contents. Substantial project progress has been achieved and impressive achievements as evidenced by demonstration of system implementation, usabilities, and utility. Substantial majority of claims are strongly supported by detailed and valid evidences. Good understanding of the user requirements and cohesive user stories, and feasible system/solution specification and design.

Addresses some of the criteria, the presentation is overall clear and articulations on some of the required aspects and contents are provided. rubric.description: Feasible plan and risk mitigation strategy for the next project stage (10%)
rubric.long_description: Feasible plan and risk mitigation strategy for the next project stage to ensure a successful completion of the project and timely delivery of the expected project outcome to the client. Identification of the prospective risks and constraints and the corresponding mitigation strategy. Challenges / Risk analysis Limitations in terms of functionality, structure, design, implementation... Technical and other constraints (for example, reliability, security,...)  Technical Constraints refer to a technology-related condition or event that prevents the project from fully delivering the optimal solution to the client, customers or end-users. Group&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;s mitigation strategy List of user stories not completed/implemented/discarded/merged with justifications and rationale. Key changes requested by the client, especially after the first client deployment, and how these changes were handled or implemented as improvements/features.  Any other details that demonstrate the group went beyond the approved scope and the bare minimum.  Feasible plan and schedule for the final project accomplishment and delivery.

ratings.long_description: Careful and thorough plan and schedule with detailed justification on feasibility; and clearly identify the risks and correspondingly propose detailed mitigation strategy to ensure the successful completion and delivery of the project as per the project statement and scope. All the marking criteria being fully addressed.

Good plan and schedule with some detailed justification on feasibility; and clearly identify the risks and correspondingly propose some mitigation strategy to ensure good-quality completion and delivery of the project as per the project statement and scope. Substantial majority of the marking criteria being fully addressed.

Reasonably good plan and schedule but with light justification on feasibility; and partially identify the risks and the proposed mitigation strategy is not substantial, which may pose concern on the successful completion and delivery of the project as per the project statement and scope. Some of the marking criteria are not properly addressed.

Brief plan and schedule with light justification on feasibility; and partially identify the risks and propose brief mitigation strategy, which may pose concerns on the successful completion and delivery of the project as per the project statement and scope. Some of the marking criteria are not properly addressed.

Fail to provide reasonable plan and schedule, missing justification on feasibility; and fail to identify the risks, and missing mitigation strategy, which pose substantial concerns on the completion and delivery of the project as per the project statement and scope. Fail to address marking criteria. The contents are not relevant or primarily generated by AI.

rubric.description: Documentation Organization & Writing - GitHub & This Report (5%)
rubric.long_description:
The project report should follow a logical structure and adhere to professional standards and practices. Evaluates professional presentation metrics, cross-referencing, hyperlinking execution, page limits, and ease of navigation.































• The individual contributions table should be included.































• The structure of GitHub site and the documents (uploaded or directly written) should be well-organised and easy-to-read.































• All the documentations should be well written in English and of a good quality, with no typos or grammatical errors.































• The relevance between the evidence and the corresponding claim should be clear and obvious and the evidence should be clear and valid.































• It should be easy for readers to find the corresponding evidence.































• A broader range of tools utilized for managing user stories, testing, group management, client interaction.































• Make sure all claims are supported by the corresponding valid evidence and they are consistent.































• All links throughout the documents should be hyperlinked and cross-referenced rather than providing the complete URL.































• Any broken/unreachable link will not be considered as evidence. Any evidence based on blurry image will not be considered. All tables, figures, diagrams, images should be numbered and captioned.































• All documents status report, meeting minutes, scope statement…etc should be in a format that does not have to be downloaded to view e.g. screenshot, image, link …etc.































• Page limits:































o Report: 25 pages































o Appendix: 10 pages































o Word size: 12

ratings.long_description:
The project report is exemplary, definitive, and adheres perfectly to the highest professional and publication-ready presentation standards.  
Report is written in precise, highly accurate presentation and terms without typos or grammatical errors.  The mandatory individual contributions table is seamlessly embedded. The GitHub repository site navigation is immaculately organized, clean, and highly intuitive to read and traverse.  All external documentation, meeting logs, and status reports are displayed directly inline or via embedded viewer links, eliminating any forced document downloads.  All links are active, clean, and structurally polished (utilizing custom hyperlinked text rather than raw URLs). All tables, figures, and diagrams are cleanly numbered and captioned.  Exacting adherence to layout boundaries: Report is within the page limits and all requirements. (Any raw URLs, broken hyperlinks, or layout limit violations result in immediate forfeiture of this top score).

Well-written and highly professional report structure with only minor formatting anomalies or isolated typos.  The GitHub site is clear and well-arranged for a reader to navigate.  All tables and figures are numbered, and documentation links function properly without forcing unnecessary downloads. Strict compliance with page and font limits is maintained.

Report is fully readable and understandable, but contains scattered layout inconsistencies, minor grammatical slips, or raw URLs instead of clean hyperlinks.  Some documents require downloading to view rather than being displayed cleanly as links or screenshots. Report complies with page and font size constraints.

The project's Documentation Organization & Writing shows a few of the criteria but misses out a major portion OR/AND there are flaws in the explanation of the criteria. Poorly organized document layout or a disorganized, hard-to-navigate GitHub site layout.  Contains multiple broken links, uncaptioned figures, or directly violates page constraints and font size formatting guidelines.

The project Documentation Organization & Writing fails to show 
and meet most of the following criteria. Incoherent organization, extensive grammatical failures that obscure meaning, broken formatting styles, or complete disregard for layout instructions and page limits. The writing is not comprehensible or  primarily generated by AI.
